title: Codes, Code Systems, and Terminology
description: Clinical logic runs on coded data. Declare code systems and named codes, match codings by BOTH code and system, and count conditions per terminology — the pattern behind every diabetes/hypertension eCQM criterion.
learningObjectives: Match a coding by code AND system (the safe pattern)
Understand why system matching matters (same code, different meaning)

hints.message: exists([Condition] C where exists(C.code.coding cod where cod.code = "Diabetes SNOMED".code and cod.system = "Diabetes SNOMED".system)) — match BOTH fields.
Same pattern with "T2DM ICD" — patient-a has an ICD E11.9 condition.
Count([Condition] C where exists(C.code.coding cod where cod.system = 'http://snomed.info/sct')) — compare the system URL directly.
The ICD-10-CM system URL is http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/icd-10-cm — patient-b's hypertension is coded in ICD, not SNOMED.
First([Condition] C where exists(...SNOMED...) return First(C.code.coding).display) — navigate into the first coding of the matching condition.
A declared code carries its display: "Diabetes SNOMED".display — it's the display YOU wrote in the declaration.
C.code.coding.code contains "Diabetes SNOMED".code — system-agnostic match. Convenient, but risky across terminologies.
Count([Condition] C return Count(C.code.coding)) — a query with return can build per-row values; Alice has 3 conditions.
Match SNOMED 38341003 (hypertension): patient-b's hypertension is ICD I10 — so SNOMED-only matching misses it. The result should be false for everyone.
